attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No explicit target-clean carrier is known with q,rho<1+epsilon, e_eff>=1+epsilon-o(1), and a non-natural N^{1+epsilon} lower bound against general circuits.
steps: Fix K_N with ordinary gates plus SAT oracle gates g=1,...,t_N, t_N<=N^q, query length L_N=(log N)^d, and overhead size N^rho.
Assume SAT has circuits C_L of size L^c. Replace every SAT gate by C_{L_N}; the resulting H_N circuit has size N^rho+t_NL_N^c=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
Thus an eventual lower bound H_N notin SIZE(N^{1+epsilon}) contradicts SAT in SIZE(n^c) for each fixed c if max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.

Audit the source claim without assuming SAT circuits. For each oracle position g, replace SAT on the finite image R_{g,N} by a DNF table for satisfiable members of R_{g,N}, costing O(|R_{g,N}|L_N), or by exhaustive assignment enumeration, costing 2^{v_N}poly(L_N).
Summing over positions gives H_N in size O(N^rho)+poly(L_N) sum_g min{|R_{g,N}|,2^{v_N}}.
Therefore any proposed source lower bound with max{rho,e_eff}<1+epsilon by a margin is internally inconsistent; high positioned effective entropy becomes a necessary certificate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a valid conditional bridge and a falsifier, not P != NP; the decisive source lower bound and nonuniform-leakage certificate remain unproved.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: positioned-range entropy audit

assumptions: There is a fixed epsilon>0 and an explicit family H_N with H_N notin SIZE(N^{1+epsilon}) for all large valid N.
The compact oracle circuit K_N has size at most N^rho and at most N^q oracle gates, with rho,q<1+epsilon.
For every oracle gate g, R_{g,N} is the set of length-L_N formulas that appear at that gate over all H_N inputs.
The source model is ordinary nonuniform Boolean circuits on N input bits, not a restricted Gamma model unless explicitly restated.
definitions: source object: an explicit length-N Boolean family H_N computed by a compact oracle circuit K_N with at most t_N=N^q SAT gates, each querying a formula of length L_N=(log N)^d over v_N variables.
target object: nonuniform SAT circuits; the target consequence is SAT notin P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly, only after the route bridge hypotheses are proven.
controlled interface: replace each SAT oracle gate of K_N either by a target SAT circuit of size L_N^c or by an unconditional per-position simulation using its image range or variable assignments.

target-preserving condition: K_N is uniform enough to name H_N, has no advice table encoding SAT answers, and satisfies max{rho,q}<1+epsilon while the source lower bound is against ordinary SIZE(N^{1+epsilon}) circuits.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No gap for affine sketches under the stated assumptions. The remaining gap is applicability: many proposed lower-bound arguments are not honestly affine-sketch objects or hide nonuniform query descriptions.
steps: Fix the accepting transcript tau of the affine verifier on the SAT truth table L_m.
Along tau, adaptivity disappears: each query vector and affine offset is now a fixed explicit row.
The set of truth tables producing tau is the solution set of at most q affine equations over F2.
A rank-r affine subspace has density 2^{-r}; since r<=q, density is at least 2^{-q}.
Membership is tested by recomputing the q affine forms on the supplied truth table, giving poly(N) constructivity under the row-uniformity assumption.
Completeness gives L_m in P_tau; universal soundness gives no SIZE(m^k) truth table in P_tau.
Therefore q<=a log N yields an N^{-a}-large constructive property useful against SIZE(m^k), so the route hits the natural-proof barrier under standard PRF hypotheses.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a barrier-transfer lemma, not SAT hardness. It certifies that one class of proof objects is invalid as a P != NP route unless it escapes through nonlinearity, superlogarithmic queries, nonconstructivity, or a non-natural feature with a separate target-preserving certificate.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: adaptive affine-sketch naturalization gate

assumptions: Truth tables are indexed over m-bit inputs; N=2^m is the natural-property input length.
Each query answer is an affine functional <a_i,f>+c_i over F2; adaptivity may depend only on previous answers.
The separator rejects every small-circuit truth table, not merely most circuits under a distribution.
The coefficient generator for query vectors is explicit enough that membership in P_tau is decidable from the full truth table in poly(N) time.
definitions: source object: poly(N)-uniform deterministic adaptive affine-sketch separator V_m for SAT truth tables f in {0,1}^N, N=2^m, using q(m) parity/affine queries over F2.
target object: Razborov-Rudich style natural property P_m subset {0,1}^N with poly(N) constructivity, inverse-polynomial largeness when q=O(log N), and usefulness against SIZE(m^k).
controlled interface: fix the accepting transcript tau of V_m on L_m; freeze the adaptive affine query rows chosen along tau; define P_tau by the resulting affine constraints and accepting leaf.

target-preserving condition: V_m has exact completeness on L_m, universal soundness against all SIZE(m^k) truth tables, and a uniform row/coefficient generator running in polynomial time in N without hidden advice.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a route-specific bridge lemma from a named source model, adaptive affine sketches, to a named target barrier object, natural properties. It strengthens the prior bit-query leaf audit to global linear queries.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Adaptive affine-sketch SAT separators with q=O(log N) queries naturalize. Let L_m be the SAT truth table on m-bit inputs, N=2^m. If a poly(N)-uniform deterministic verifier makes q adaptive affine F2 queries to an oracle truth table f, accepts L_m, and rejects every truth table computed by SIZE(m^k) circuits, then the accepting transcript for L_m defines a poly(N)-constructive property of density at least 2^{-q} containing L_m and useful against SIZE(m^k). Thus global parity queries are not a valid natural-proof escape at logarithmic query complexity.

Soundness still excludes all size-s circuit truth tables if usefulness is to transfer.

target model: natural-property transfer requiring constructivity, largeness, and usefulness against SIZE(m^k).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: This does not construct any high-MCSP source; it only gives a necessary anti-checkpoint condition. A source might use large space sigma or nonlocal global computation, so the lemma is an obstruction, not a completeness theorem.
steps: Fix an accepted certificate z and emitted table y of length N=2^m.
Choose checkpoint spacing B. Hardwire in a Boolean circuit all configurations of V_m(z) immediately before output positions 0,B,2B,... . This costs about (N/B)S(m) bits/gates up to indexing overhead.

On input i in {0,1}^m, compute q=floor(i/B) and r=i-qB, select the hardwired q-th configuration, and simulate V for r<=B output steps to recover y_i. This costs B poly(m) gates for a fixed universal transition implementation.
Therefore y has circuits of size O((N/B)S(m)+B poly(m)); optimizing gives O(sqrt(N S(m) poly(m))).
If S(m)=2^{sigma m+o(m)}, every accepted output has circuits of size 2^{((1+sigma)/2)m+o(m)}. A claimed MCSP no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m} is impossible when epsilon>(1+sigma)/2 plus margin.
The carrier-to-E extraction remains valid only after choosing epsilon below this universal upper bound and below any stronger indexed replay scheme present in the proposed source.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The main conjecture is untouched. Even the route-level lower bound still requires an actual sparse, uniform, sound, non-natural certificate source satisfying MCSP(y)>2^{epsilon m} for a constant epsilon that survives checkpoint leakage.

branch_outputs.branch_title: MCSP / Meta-Complexity Carrier Transfer, cycle 17: space-sensitive checkpoint leakage

assumptions: V is deterministic after fixing m and z; randomized certificates require fixing all coins or adding them to z.
The nonuniform circuit for y_i may hardwire checkpoint configurations, since MCSP measures ordinary nonuniform circuit size of the emitted table.
Configuration length S(m) includes work tapes, head positions, m, z, and finite control; if V uses exponential space, the checkpoint bound weakens accordingly.
The bridge consequence is route-level only: it gives an E lower bound if the source exists; it is not a proof of P != NP.
definitions: source object: a uniform deterministic verifier V_m(z) with |z|=O(m) that emits a truth table y in {0,1}^{N}, N=2^m, in time N poly(m) or 2^{O(m)}, and whose sound accepted outputs are intended to satisfy MCSP(y)>K(m).

target object: an E-uniform language L whose length-m truth tables are the accepted y_m on kappa-dense source lengths, yielding nonuniform circuit lower bounds SIZE(2^{delta n}) for every delta<epsilon/kappa after padding/interpolation.

controlled interface: the only information passed from the MCSP carrier to the target is a uniformly searchable accepted certificate plus a sound no-side lower bound MCSP(y_m)>2^{epsilon m}; no nonuniform selector or external truth-table advice may enter.

target-preserving condition: certificate search, output indexing, and length interpolation must run in 2^{O(n)} time, preserve kappa-density, and keep the MCSP threshold exponent epsilon constant enough that delta<epsilon/kappa remains positive.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed source has S(m)=poly(m) and claims epsilon>=1/2, the generic checkpoint circuit is a falsifier; if it has indexed checkpoints with total storage plus replay below 2^{epsilon m}, its MCSP no-side soundness is invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the restart/checkpoint concern into a quantitative obstruction and repairs the route by adding a space exponent parameter to the source model.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Space-sensitive checkpoint leakage lemma: an O(m)-certificate sequential MCSP no-side source whose accepted table is emitted by a deterministic verifier with configuration length S(m) has nonuniform circuits of size O((N/B)S(m)+B poly(m)) for every checkpoint spacing B. Hence a valid source claiming MCSP threshold K(m)=2^{epsilon m} must defeat every indexed checkpoint/replay tradeoff below K(m); in particular polyspace streaming sources cannot support epsilon >= 1/2.

assumptions: At least one valid certificate exists on each source length in the kappa-dense set.
All accepted certificates are sound no-side witnesses, not merely most certificates.
The verifier and search rule are uniform and do not depend on advice selecting hard tables.
definitions: source model: sparse sequential MCSP certificate source with no accepted output admitting subthreshold indexed replay.
target class: E against nonuniform Boolean circuits of size 2^{delta n}.
density parameter: every target length n has a source length m in [n,n^kappa] after the fixed padding map.
explicitness parameter: the lexicographically first accepted certificate is found by exhaustive search in 2^{O(m)} time.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Keeps the previously valid extraction theorem but records the new space/checkpoint side condition required for source soundness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Space-repaired carrier bridge: if a sparse uniform certificate source has O(m)-bit certificates, verifier time 2^{O(m)}, kappa-dense source lengths, and soundness MCSP(y_m)>2^{epsilon m} with epsilon below all available checkpoint upper bounds, then exhaustive E search extracts an E language requiring circuits 2^{delta n} for every delta<epsilon/kappa.

assumptions: The accepted-table set is sparse and syntactically tied to certificates.
No pseudorandom-function-breaking largeness conclusion is inferred from the sparse source alone.
definitions: source property: set of truth tables accepted by V_m with some O(m)-bit certificate.
largeness estimate: at most 2^{O(m)} accepted certificates produce at most 2^{O(m)} accepted tables among 2^{2^m} possible tables.
constructivity estimate: membership in the carrier property is searchable in 2^{O(m)}, not necessarily decidable in poly(N).

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates this branch from folklore barrier restatement: sparsity avoids immediate naturalness, while checkpoint leakage remains the active nonuniform obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Barrier-status lemma: the sparse certificate-source route is not automatically large in the Razborov-Rudich sense, but every dense or locally decidable repair becomes natural-proof-like unless it proves non-largeness or nonconstructivity explicitly.

The next work should search for a sparse non-natural source at a checkpoint-safe epsilon, not restate P != NP or hardness magnification folklore.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier soundness must include resistance to indexed checkpoint/replay circuits of size below 2^{epsilon m}; sequentiality alone is too weak.
The E extraction from O(m)-certificate kappa-dense no-side carriers remains valid once epsilon survives checkpoint upper bounds.
Explicitness is exhaustive E search over sparse certificates; it must not include a nonuniform selector for hard truth tables.
